New wire stories this morning (Fed Governor Waller on rate hikes, oil and gold moves, Nvidia pre-market) could not be opened and checked, so they are left out.
headline: SA unemployment edges up to 33.7% in Q3; JSE adds about 0.4% by late morning while Brent slips to $90.18 ahead of US CPI
summary: Stats SA's Q3 jobs survey put unemployment at 33.7%, up from 33.6% in Q2 (Stats SA via eNCA, 10 Nov), while the JSE All Share was at 115,514.94 (+0.4%) and the rand steady at R16.37/$ at 11:41 SAST (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov). On Wall Street the S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,549.94 (+2.3%) and the Nasdaq at 25,253.14 (+2.7%), with Nvidia down 4.3% after the FBI comments on its CEO (Yahoo Finance, 9 Nov; Al Jazeera, 10 Nov). Brent gave back a further 1.7% to $90.18 and gold eased 0.6% to $4,098 by late morning (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov), with US October CPI at 15:30 SAST the next big test for the rand and miners.

items.title: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese agent
items.summary: Speaking at the White House on Monday, President Trump said the FBI is probing Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US officials allege worked for Chinese intelligence; Trump said Huang told him he had no idea and that he believes him. Nvidia's board opened an independent inquiry on Sunday and said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised; China's foreign ministry called the reports groundless. This is the background to Monday's 4.27% fall to $178.67, a week before Nvidia's 17 November results; the LRC rating (HOLD) is unchanged (Al Jazeera, 10 Nov 2026).

items.title: AMD closes +13.3% at $508.58; Nvidia closes -4.3% at $178.67
items.summary: AMD extended its intraday gain into the close on Monday 9 November, while Nvidia (HOLD) fell 4.3% and stays below its $191.50 breakdown level ahead of results on 17 November. The reasons behind Nvidia's fall could not be verified for this edition and are left out.
